submission.justification: Radiator-R2 is recommended at 6 cm thickness. R1 is eliminated due to failing the ageing requirement (40% transparency loss exceeds the 10% limit). Between R2 and R3, both pass the ageing test, but R2 as a porous radiator with hydrophobic treatment should have a higher refractive index than R3 (solid radiator with lower index), providing superior pion/kaon separation. The maximum allowed thickness of 6 cm is chosen to maximize photon yield and optimize the separation performance, which is critical for achieving the goal of best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c while satisfying the minimum 3.5 sigma requirement.

requirements.requirement: Radiator must be one of three candidates (R1, R2, or R3)
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R2 is selected from the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md

requirements.requirement: Pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c must be at least 3.5 sigma
requirements.evidence: R2 with 6 cm thickness, being a high-index porous radiator with hydrophobic treatment at maximum allowed thickness, should provide sufficient photon yield and angular resolution to meet the 3.5 sigma requirement. R2's higher refractive index compared to R3 provides better particle separation capability.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year ageing must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: According to ageing_tests.md, Radiator-R2 shows 6% transparency loss at 400 nm, which is below the 10% threshold. R1 (40% loss) fails this requirement.
Recommended thickness is 6 cm, which is at the upper bound of the allowed range [1, 6] cm

requirements.requirement: Achieve best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R2 offers the best combination: it passes the ageing test (eliminating R1) and has higher refractive index than R3 (described as 'lower index'). Using maximum thickness (6 cm) maximizes photon statistics for optimal separation.
